subject: ACME POC — evaluation methodology & success criteria
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC — post-demo recap and next steps

Hi Sara/Tom,

Thanks again for the demo today — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment before the POC kickoff:

- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for ACME’s customer support summarization pipeline (30M tokens/month, 95th pct latency < 500ms).
- Success criteria (draft): 1) extractive+abstractive summaries meet ACME QA pass rate >= 90% on the evaluation rubric; 2) infra supports sustained 2 RPS with <500ms 95th latency; 3) model cost target <= $0.002/token equivalent.
- Evaluation scope: 1 week offline evaluation (sampled historical tickets) + 2-week online shadow (non-production) run to confirm latency and stability.
- Ownership: ACME will provide sample dataset and rubric; Redwood will provide eval harness, baseline outputs, and support for online shadowing.
- Proposed timeline: share success criteria & rubric by Wed 3/17, start offline eval week of 3/22, online shadow 4/1-4/14.

I'll attach draft success criteria and a simple rubric. Can you confirm the timeline and who on your side will own the sample data and scoring?

Thanks,
— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ACME_POC_Success_Criteria.pdf (PDF, 128KB)]

From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@acme.com>

Subject: Re: ACME POC — post-demo recap and next steps

Hey Dylan — thanks for the clear recap. This looks good overall. A few quick notes:

- Timeline: Wed 3/17 for rubric works. Our data owner (Tom) will assemble a de-identified sample set (~1k tickets) by Fri 3/19. Offline eval week of 3/22 is fine.
- Ownership: Tom will own data and initial scoring coordination. I'll own overall success sign-off.
- Security: Looping in ACME IT Security for the shadow run details — we need an IP allowlist and contract addendum for data handling. Security, any concerns?

One question on evaluation methodology: we prefer an offline blind scoring as the primary signal, with a short online shadow to validate infra metrics. We want to avoid full online A/B in the POC. Can Redwood describe the difference between your offline eval harness and the online shadow approach (what's graded in each)?

Best,
Sara
Head of Product, ACME Corp

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — post-demo recap and next steps

Thanks Sara — great questions. Short answer up-front:

- Offline eval: we run your de-identified sample against candidate model variants, produce outputs, and provide a grading UI + baseline scoring using your rubric. Metrics graded offline = semantic accuracy, factuality, brevity, and QA pass/fail. This is the authority for qualitative quality decisions.
- Online shadow: we route real traffic copies (no customer-facing changes) to Redwood in parallel to your prod model to measure latency, memory/KV cache behavior, tail-latency, and error/retry profiles in your environment. We also capture per-request tokens & cost estimates. Online shadow is primarily for infra/ops validation, not primary quality grading.

Attached is a simple grading rubric template and an outline of the offline eval steps + what we capture during the online shadow. For the POC I recommend: offline -> pick 1 model variant that meets quality threshold -> 2-week shadow to validate infra & runbook.

If that approach looks good, we'll finalize the rubric by Wed and I’ll have Marissa (our evaluation lead) pull the harness and run the offline job next week.

— Dylan
[Attachment: evaluation_rubric.xlsx (Excel, 22KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME POC — eval plan (offline vs shadow)

Quick sync for internal alignment before we send the final rubric to ACME:

- Offline eval details: Marissa to run 1 full pass with 1k de-identified tickets (stratified by ticket type). Produce per-case scores (semantic accuracy, hallucination score, brevity, QA pass). We'll compute pass-rate and per-metric distributions. Deliverable: offline eval report + CSV with judged rows.
- Shadow run details: Rachel to own infra validation runbook (network, token accounting, latency dashboards). We'll collect 95/99/avg latency, memory usage, error rates, and ops playbook validation. Deliverable: shadow dashboard and incident runbook.
- Rubric: use the attached template; add explicit thresholds for critical fields (e.g., hallucination tolerance <= 1% on sampled cases).

Action items:
- Marissa: set up offline job upon ACME data receipt (owner: marissa.cole).
- Rachel: prepare shadow dashboards and a short ops checklist (owner: rachel.kim).
- Dylan: send final rubric and timeline to ACME wed morning.

Thanks — I’ll be available for a quick huddle if needed.

— Marissa
Principal ML Ops, Redwood Inference
